summary: Daybreak Coffee Co. sounds like your funniest friend who happens to be a coffee nerd: lowercase, pun-happy, emoji-rich and never snobby. Coffee is described by what it tastes like in plain words, and every email has a joke or two.
audience: Coffee lovers aged 22–40 who want great coffee without being lectured about it.

tone_by_email_type.tone: Excited and jokey, with the deal stated clearly in caps once (FREE) and a playful deadline.
Club-membership framing, checklist of perks, self-deprecating pun apology.
Teasing personification of the beans, a nudge about free shipping.
Magazine-style sections with emoji headers, farm story, brewing hack, office joke.
Hype-y but honest; plays on customer excitement, lists quirky facts.
Inviting and explanatory; demystifies coffee jargon.

mechanics.sentence_length: Short and conversational; mix of full sentences and quick asides in parentheses.
mechanics.person: "we" for the crew, "you" for the reader; occasionally names team members (Maya, Kevin the roaster).
mechanics.capitalization: lowercase subject lines, greetings and most body copy; product and people names keep capitals; one word in CAPS for emphasis.
mechanics.punctuation: Exclamation points allowed but never stacked; parentheses for jokes; colons before lists.
mechanics.emoji: Freely: one at the end of the subject line, as list bullets, and in section headers.
mechanics.formatting: Emoji-bulleted lists, short sections, one button, casual sign-off.

patterns: lowercase pun + one emoji at the end
playful personification ("your coffee is getting cold")
subject_lines.typical_length: 25–45 characters, lowercase, ends with one emoji
examples: buy one bag, get one bean-efit 🎁
welcome to the good mornings club ☕

patterns: Explains the pun or adds the offer detail
examples: BOGO on every 12 oz bag this weekend. yes, even the fancy ones.
well, technically it's still beans. but you get the idea.

patterns: lowercase, playful, 2–4 words, often personifies the beans

dos: Describe flavour in everyday words (tastes like berries)
Mention fresh roasting on Mondays when relevant
Keep the tone inclusive: any way you drink coffee is fine
donts: Sound snobby or use coffee jargon without explaining it
Stack three or more puns in one line
